### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), handleRequest (symbol, a method of class AuthManager; a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), handleRequest (symbol, a method of class AuthManager; a top-level function), internalAdapter (symbol, a field of interface SamlLandingContext))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via error_description (literal, a string literal in rebaseSamlRefusal), /sso/saml2/sp/acs/:providerId (route, a path literal in a comment in AuthManager; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via internalAdapter (symbol, a field of interface SamlLandingContext))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a1b070c91b1bab22da8a8644ffc6d024eafc268d` — the merge of head `ffdd6e0fc391d8ca76cf9aba4a490d1852563942` into base `065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a1b070c91b1bab22da8a8644ffc6d024eafc268d && git checkout a1b070c91b1bab22da8a8644ffc6d024eafc268d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596 ffdd6e0fc391d8ca76cf9aba4a490d1852563942 && git checkout -B drift-repro 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596 && git merge --no-ff ffdd6e0fc391d8ca76cf9aba4a490d1852563942

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-07T19:20Z · head `ffdd6e0fc391d8ca76cf9aba4a490d1852563942`

Seat `domain:server#6` reviewed the diff of its own dispatch (claim 6710984037 on #30966, card thread `session_01FEkQ5mjnQAcpdnyqK2Xi6y`, report 6711645407). Read against GitHub, not the report.

1. **Shape:** 6 files, +639 / -20. The SAML ACS (`POST /sso/saml2/sp/acs/:providerId`) now runs inside the same refusal scope as the OIDC callback (#31194's seam): `ssoCallbackOf` picks OIDC or SAML-POST, `runSsoCallbackScope` keeps the OIDC branch as it was, and for SAML reads the relay-state row (`auth-state:<RelayState>`) through the vendor's own `internalAdapter` BEFORE the vendor consumes it. A vendor redirect carrying `error=` that is not the success URL is re-based onto the error URL, keeping `error` / `error_description`; success, IdP-initiated (no relay state), and unreadable state are left as the vendor answered. The error URL passes the vendor's redirect safety rule again (`safeSamlTarget`: no `//`, `/\`, encoded variants, foreign untrusted origin, or the ACS itself). Host member renamed `runSsoOidcCallback` → `runSsoCallback` (private). No vendored patch. Docs: one step added to the SAML flow in `sso.mdx`. Body says `Fixes #30966`; no other closing keyword.
2. **Premise:** on `origin/main` an account refusal from `handleOAuthUserInfo` (`account_not_linked` and five siblings) lands on the success `callbackURL` with only `?error=`, and an over-size response lands on the app origin; red reproduced at `66bf5b4a` per the report, and the new test file's takeover / over-size cases pin both.
3. **Gates / check-runs:** 50 runs on this head, 38 success, 12 skipped, 0 red, including Test Core 1–8/8, Type Check · workspace and Lint. `mergeable_state` clean. Dev: plugin-auth 236/236 files green, 95/95 derived gates exit 0 (`pm-orders/server/30966-gates-ran.txt`), three ablations red and restored.
4. **Accepted deviations / notes:** with no `errorCallbackURL`, a refused SAML sign-in now lands on the platform error page (`onAPIError.errorURL`, the Console sign-in page) instead of the signed-in page; that is where OIDC and every other SAML refusal already land, and the PR's Acceptance notes and the changeset say so. Accepted as the fix itself.
5. **Out of scope / Skills-docs:** the SAML refusal CAUSE (vendor's bare `catch` around `parseLoginResponse`) still waits on the vendor, as the module doc says; #31168 untouched. `Metadata-protocol: none`; `Skills-docs:` not owed. Nothing filed.
6. **Landing:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31231`: not governed, 659 changed lines. `Clause-②: no` (the package's named exports from `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.ts` are unchanged; only the `Location` of a refusal 302 moves), no `packages/spec/src` path, so no contract review is owed. Changeset `30966-saml-refusal-lands-on-error-url.md`, patch, holds. Landing on the maintainer's standing words 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」 (2026-10-25T11:35Z) and 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-07T16:59Z). Relay `pr_ready`, then `automerge_enable`.
